title: Veolia selects Legora to power AI-enabled legal work across its global legal function
summary: Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work, today announced a collaboration with Veolia, the global benchmark company for ecological transformation, to support Veolia's Group Legal function with an AI-enabled workflow across day-to-day legal tasks.
body_markdown:
"Veolia's legal teams look forward to using the power and strength of Legora's systems and tools to increase our efficiency and reinforce our sharing of know-how and best practices," said Eric Haza, Chief Legal Officer at Veolia. "Legora will accelerate our ability to process documentation, thereby freeing time to concentrate on value-added strategic and business deal considerations."


Founded in 1853, Veolia employs close to 215,000 people worldwide and generated nearly €45 billion in revenue in 2025 across water, waste, and energy management. Its Group Legal function matches that scale: a multi-region organisation spanning Europe, working in both English and French, the Americas, and Asia-Pacific, managing high volumes of legal work while staying aligned with global standards.


That is the environment Legora is being built into. In-house teams at organisations of Veolia's size face the same pressure as everyone else in legal: higher workloads, faster turnaround expectations, constant regulatory change, but multiplied across jurisdictions, languages, and time zones. The collaboration is designed to help Veolia's legal professionals reduce time spent on repetitive work and focus more on strategic, high-judgment matters, with humans firmly in control of review and decisions throughout.


Through the collaboration, Veolia's legal teams will bring knowledge, drafting, and review workflows together in one place, work with greater speed and consistency across regions and languages, and free up time from repetitive, high-volume tasks for strategic and business-critical work.


The rollout has been shaped to fit how Veolia actually operates, including a Google Workspace-first setup, so the platform slots into existing ways of working rather than asking teams to change how they collaborate. Legora will be introduced in phases, pairing access with structured onboarding and training, and both teams are aligned on governance and enablement, with clear internal roles and a training programme designed to help users build confidence quickly.


For Legora, this marks one of its most significant enterprise engagements to date: a global industrial leader bringing agentic AI into the core of its legal function, across regions and languages, with governance and training built in from the start.


"Veolia is one of the largest and most complex organisations in the world, and its legal function reflects that: multiple regions, multiple languages, and a volume of work most teams never see," said Max Junestrand, CEO and Co-Founder of Legora. "That they chose to bring Legora into the core of how their lawyers work every day, with governance and training built in from the start, says a lot about where in-house legal is heading. We're proud to be building this with them."


About Veolia


Veolia group is the benchmark company for ecological transformation. With close to 215,000 employees worldwide, the Group designs and provides game-changing solutions that are both useful and practical for water, waste, and energy management. Through its three complementary business activities, Veolia helps develop access to resources, protect available resources, and replenish them. In 2025, the Veolia group generated revenue of nearly €45 billion.


About Legora


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 130,000 legal professionals at more than 2,000 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 80 markets.
